grades.notes: Here compressive 0.2% yield is about 12-14 percent BELOW the vendor tensile 0.2% yield (37.1-38.1 vs 42.8-43.3 ksi), opposite to Materion's 'typically 10% higher' statement. Different test labs, strain rates and specimen orientation (tension transverse to pressing; compression orientation not stated). Report text: 'Beyond the yield points, i.e., after a few percent strain, the tension and compression curves are in reasonably good agreement.' The yield-point drop phenomenon (upper/lower yield) is present in tension and appears in compression as inflections. Elongation 2.7 taken as the lower of the vendor's 3.2 and 2.7. Tensile yield Pa/ultimate Pa use the higher of the two vendor values (43.3, 58.0 ksi). Material is block, not sheet.

statements.source: Materion, A Guide to Designing and Fabricating with Beryllium, PDF p.4
statements.quote: The compressive yield strength (0.2% offset) at room temperature of beryllium is typically 10% higher than the tensile yield strength. At 400°F (204°C), the compressive yield strength remains about equal to the tensile yield strength. This is a unique property of beryllium and is demonstrated by S-200-F, where the room temperature tensile yield strength and compressive yield strength are about 37 ksi (255 MPa).
statements.caveat: Maker prose, no lot, no sheet. Two of three measured comparisons found here (S-200E block 1973; extruded tube 1968) show compressive yield equal to or BELOW tensile 0.2% yield, and the SR-200 sheet shows them equal within 1.1 percent. Use equal (ratio 1.0) as the evidence-supported value for design; the 'typically 10% higher' is not reproduced by any test table found.

statements.source: Roschke et al., NASA CR-194164 (1991), Table 3 after Fenn et al. 1967
statements.quote: Longitudinal Tension 383.4 537.6; Compression 379.2 659.1 | Long transverse Tension 386.1 564.0; Compression 382.7 591.5 (Yield Stress MPa, Ultimate Stress MPa)

statements.topic: compressive vs tensile ULTIMATE strength, SR-200 sheet
statements.source: Roschke et al., NASA CR-194164 (1991), section 5.2.1
statements.quote: In each case, compressive strength is approximately 20% higher than the tensile strength in the same direction, which is characteristic of brittle material. Although beryllium is ductile when undergoing an in-plane tensile load, compressive loadings manifest very different behavior. Results obtained suggest that the material exhibits brittle properties for compressive in-plane loadings.
statements.caveat: About ULTIMATE (failure) stress in a 12.7 mm unsupported-length sheet compression coupon: 658.8 MPa (95.6 ksi) parallel and 691.8 MPa (100.3 ksi) perpendicular to primary rolling, 2.54 mm sheet; the specimens 'fail catastrophically'. It is not a yield statement and says compression failure of this sheet is brittle.

statements.topic: tension vs compression curves, VHP S-200E
statements.source: Harrod et al., NASA CR-133890 (1973), section 4.1.1
statements.quote: Upper and lower yield points were observed at test temperatures up through 750°F. In the compression tests the yield drops were manifested as inflections in the load-deflection curves. Beyond the yield points, i.e., after a few percent strain, the tension and compression curves are in reasonably good agreement.

statements.source: Materion, A Guide to Designing and Fabricating with Beryllium, PDF p.8 'ROLLED BERYLLIUM SHEET AND FOIL' and 'ROLLED BERYLLIUM PLATE AND SHEET'
statements.quote: By convention, beryllium rolled stock with a gauge between 0.020" (0.51 mm) and 0.250" (6.35 mm) is known as sheet, while thicker gauge material is referred to as a plate. The specifications are SR-200 for sheet between 0.020" (0.51 mm) and 0.220" (5.56 mm) and PS-200 for sheet between 0.005" (0.13 mm) and 0.250" (6.35 mm) inclusive. The difference between the grades is that SR-200 is hot-rolled and has minimum mechanical properties. In plane tensile minimum, tensile properties are 70 ksi (483 MPa) ultimate tensile strength, 50 ksi (345 MPa), 0.2% yield strength and 10.0% elongation.
statements.caveat: Brochure gives sheet thickness up to 0.220 in for SR-200 here, while the 2024 SR-200 datasheet says 0.059 to 0.250 in made to order. PF-60 is described there as 99% Be foil, not a structural sheet. Both facts as read; the brochure's grammar is garbled in the printed text.

statements.source: Materion, A Guide to Designing and Fabricating with Beryllium, PDF p.5
statements.quote: Beryllium has a modulus of elasticity of 44.0 msi (303 GPa)
statements.caveat: Datasheets print 290 GPa (42 msi) as 'typical' for S-200-F, SR-200, I-220-H, S-65; Texas A&M SR-200 sheet Table 2 gives 298.7 GPa longitudinal, 293.6 GPa long-transverse, 347.5 GPa through-thickness; the same report quotes 320 GPa average in-plane compressive modulus from Aldinger (not verified).

statements.quote: S-200-FH is hot isostatic pressed beryllium which provides isotropic properties along with slightly higher density and greater strength than vacuum hot-pressed or cold isostatic pressed and sintered beryllium.

gaps: No guaranteed-minimum or typical COMPRESSIVE yield printed in any Materion datasheet (S-200-F/FC/FH, SR-200, I-70-H, I-220-H, S-65/S-65-H); only the design-guide prose gives S-200-F 'about 37 ksi (255 MPa)'.
No compressive yield for I-220-H, S-200-FH, I-70-H or any HIP grade found.

I-250 and I-400: no document found; they did not appear in any Materion page opened (Materion beryllium-metal page lists I-70-H, I-220-H, S-200-F/FC/FH, S-65/S-65-H, B-26-D, SR-200 only). Not sourced.
O-50: not found. O-30/O-30H: only a single room-temperature UTS (422.16 MPa) from a NASA paper; no yield, no Materion datasheet found.

PF-60 (99% Be foil) and PS-200 (standard-purity foil/sheet) Materion datasheets were opened (optimizely downloads 74b1f22a... and 74937cf0...): they carry chemistry and gauges but NO mechanical properties. PS-200 and PF-60 strengths: null.

SR-200 sheet direction-specific tensile values (Fenn 1967) are only seen second-hand via Roschke 1991; AFML-TR-67-212 itself not located/opened. The Materion SR-200 datasheet gives only an in-plane minimum without direction.

DTIC documents (AD0813757, AD0463896, AD0855716, ADA147788, AD0405939, AD0871166) returned an HTML challenge page (HTTP 403 for WebFetch) and were NOT read. Search-engine snippets claiming cross-rolled sheet Fty/Fcy values from AD0813757 are therefore unverified and not used.
MIL-HDBK-5/MMPDS beryllium tables: not found or opened.

Matmatch, UL Prospector, AZoM and ASM Alloy Digest pages appeared in search results; Matmatch/Prospector not opened, ASM Alloy Digest S-200F page is paywalled (abstract only), AZoM page opened but has no grade or form (tensile 370 MPa, yield 240 MPa, E 303 GPa, density 1.844 g/cm3 generic) so it was excluded.
No thickness-dependent sheet data or minimum compressive/buckling-relevant (tangent modulus) data found for cross-rolled sheet other than the 1.96 mm and 2.54 mm SR-200 sheets in CR-194164.
Elastic modulus values for I-250/I-400/O-30 not found.
Crossref check: not applicable, no DOI was used for any source (all NTRS and Materion URLs, doi null). No value or identifier was recalled from memory.
